headline: Wall Street stages a huge rebound as Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang, Ghana's banks say cheaper loans are coming after the 11% policy rate, and Article 6 carbon-market rules come through COP31 intact.

items.title: Russian warship reported sunk at Libya's Benghazi port
items.summary: Libya's eastern authorities say a Russian naval vessel sank at Benghazi after a suspected drone attack, with a commercial ship also hit and a few people slightly hurt. Zelensky said Ukraine was behind it; the Kremlin called a separate drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic 'terrorist activity', and the UN mission in Libya wants an independent probe.
items.why: The Ukraine war is now spilling onto African soil and shipping routes.
items.videoQuery: Russian warship sunk Benghazi Libya Ukraine drone

items.title: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukraine's Kyiv region
items.summary: Officials say a Russian attack on Dymer in the Kyiv region killed 11 people, with others missing after part of an apartment block was destroyed. Zelensky renewed calls for more US Patriot air-defence missiles.
items.videoQuery: Dymer Kyiv region Russian strike apartment

items.title: Trump to meet NATO chief Rutte on Wednesday
items.summary: The White House says Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte will meet in Palm Beach, Florida, after Trump's talks with Putin and Xi last week drew criticism from European allies. European leaders and Zelensky want Europe included in any US-backed peace talks on Ukraine.
items.videoQuery: Trump Rutte meeting Palm Beach NATO

items.title: Reactions pour in after COP31 collapses
items.summary: COP31 in Antalya is the first UN climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without an agreement. The EU and UK refused a text that did not mention fossil fuels, while Russia and Saudi Arabia resisted such wording; UN chief Guterres said he was deeply disappointed.

items.title: Article 6 rulebook survives, with a review in 2028
items.summary: Carbon Market Watch says the Article 6 rules came through COP31 unchanged despite industry pressure to loosen them, but a major review is due in 2028 and it expects the fight to resume at COP32. ClimateTrade notes 16 countries have joined a coalition to grow carbon markets, and Norway agreed to buy up to 12 million tonnes of credits from Indonesian solar projects.
items.why: The rules Ghana's Carbon Market Office uses for Article 6 deals stay stable for now: good for project planning.

items.title: Adaptation Fund now fully under the Paris Agreement
items.summary: COP31 completed the Adaptation Fund's move to serve only the Paris Agreement. It will get a mandatory 5% share of proceeds from the Article 6.4 crediting mechanism, plus voluntary money from Article 6.2 deals.
items.why: Every Article 6.4 credit sale now directly funds adaptation in poorer countries: a useful talking point with buyers.

items.title: IEA lifts Africa's renewables outlook by 54%
items.summary: The IEA's Renewables 2026 report expects sub-Saharan Africa to add over 120 GW of renewable capacity from 2026 to 2031, nearly doubling what exists, with solar making up more than 80%. Distributed solar for homes, businesses and off-grid users is set to be almost two-thirds of new solar.
items.why: Distributed solar for productive use, like cold storage for fish, is where the growth is.

items.title: Banks say loans will get cheaper after BoG's rate cut
items.summary: The Bank of Ghana cut its policy rate from 14% to 11% on 18 November, with inflation around 5.5–5.7%, well below its target band. The Ghana Association of Banks now expects lending rates to fall significantly, and says the Ghana Reference Rate could drop into single digits.
items.why: Cheaper credit could make financing ovens for processors more affordable.
items.videoQuery: Bank of Ghana policy rate cut 11 percent

items.title: Gold Fields pledges $7.5bn for Tarkwa as lease end nears
items.summary: Gold Fields Ghana says it would invest $7.5bn in the Tarkwa mine over about 20 years if its leases, which expire in April 2027, are renewed. The company says 74% of every dollar the mine earns stays in Ghana.
items.videoQuery: Gold Fields Tarkwa lease renewal Ghana

items.title: Galamsey threatens Sunyani's water supply
items.summary: The utilities regulator PURC warns that illegal mining on the upper Tano River has kept water turbidity high for three months at the Abesim treatment plant, raising treatment costs. It called for coordinated action and investment to expand the plant serving Bono and Ahafo.

items.title: Fighting in DR Congo hampers Ebola response
items.summary: WHO chief Tedros has called for peace after heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province forced Ebola responders to shelter for more than a day. The outbreak, declared in May, is still not under control.
items.videoQuery: Ebola Ituri DR Congo fighting WHO

items.title: Nasdaq jumps 6.5% as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang
items.summary: US stocks staged a huge rebound on Monday after Nvidia's board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after he resigned. Nvidia rose more than 31%, the Nasdaq gained 6.51% and the Dow added about 1,448 points, after a week in which the S&P 500 fell into a correction.
items.why: Markets still price in a likely Fed rate hike in December, which affects global investor appetite for Africa.
items.videoQuery: Nvidia Jensen Huang return stocks rally

items.title: Africa's own credit rating agency targets first ratings by March
items.summary: The African Union's new Africa Credit Rating Agency, based in Mauritius, is in talks with 15 governments and plans its first sovereign ratings by the end of March. Supporters say global agencies judge Africa too harshly; Moody's disputes that.
items.why: Credit ratings shape what Ghana, and Ghanaian projects, pay to borrow.

items.title: Brains share one meaning code across 21 languages
items.summary: MIT researchers used multilingual AI models to predict brain activity in speakers of 21 languages listening to the same story. A model trained only on French could even predict responses in Vietnamese speakers, pointing to a shared code for meaning.
items.videoQuery: MIT brain shared meaning across languages

items.title: Depression may be an early sign of Alzheimer's
items.summary: In cognitively normal older adults, faster build-up of the protein tau in the brain went with faster rises in depressive symptoms, a study in the Journal of Neuroscience found. The authors say more work is needed before mood changes can be used to predict decline.

items.title: Weight-loss drugs could free up farmland worldwide
items.summary: Modelling in Nature Communications suggests that if GLP-1 drugs cut how much people eat, up to 6.6 million deaths a year could be avoided by 2050 and about 32 million hectares of land could return to nature. The authors stress these are exploratory scenarios, not forecasts.

good.title: Ghana's Dawa gets a 100 MW solar plant
good.summary: LMI Holdings has an $88.6m financing package, including IFC and other lenders, for a 100 MW solar plant at Dawa supplying more than 95 industrial tenants. It is the first phase of a planned 200 MW.
good.why: Clean power for Ghanaian industry: the same story as clean heat for fish processors.

good.title: Kenya and DR Congo restore full diplomatic ties
good.summary: After talks in the Republic of Congo, Kenya and DR Congo agreed to bring back ambassadors and restart their joint commission.

good.title: Tunisia funds solar plus battery storage
good.summary: EBRD and the Climate Investment Funds are putting €50m into a 50 MW solar plant with a 10 MW battery at Beni Mhira in Tataouine.

good.title: Jonathan the 194-year-old tortoise reveals anti-ageing genes
good.summary: Scientists studying Jonathan, the giant tortoise on St Helena, found 287 genetic variants linked to protection from ageing.

good.title: X-ray telescope opens its eyes after 8 years in space
good.summary: The MIXS telescope on the European-Japanese BepiColombo mission to Mercury took its first images, of the Crab Nebula, with sharper resolution than in lab tests.

quiz.q: What is the Bank of Ghana's new policy rate?
quiz.why: The BoG cut its rate from 14% to 11% on 18 November.

quiz.q: COP31 was the first UN climate summit to end without agreement since which one?
quiz.why: Al Jazeera and Reuters say no COP had failed to agree since Copenhagen.

quiz.q: What share of Article 6.4 credit proceeds now goes to the Adaptation Fund?
quiz.why: COP31 confirmed a mandatory 5% share of proceeds for the Fund.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.
